We've got a natural transition point here, and I think it's a good opportunity to address some of the issues that have come up -- specifically around interruptions and improvised exercises making it harder to have candid discussions. Before we decide on any changes, I'd like to hear from each of you: what's working, what isn't, and what you'd want to see in a new format. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I can start. I think there's a lot of value in the retrospective, and having that dedicated time is important. But I've found it difficult to engage fully at times -- some of the on-the-spot exercises have been challenging for me to participate in. As we think about a new format, I'd really like to see discussion questions and prompts shared in writing ahead of time, so I can prepare and contribute meaningfully. I also think a more structured approach with less room for interruptions would help keep the conversation on track for everyone.
